text: Griseofulvin acts as a non-ATP-competitive inhibitor of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein, the constitutively active tyrosine kinase driving Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). It binds to the myristoyl-binding pocket of the ABL1 kinase domain, stabilizing the inactive conformation of the enzyme and effectively suppressing its oncogenic signaling pathways. This allosteric inhibition provides a therapeutic rationale for overcoming resistance to traditional ATP-competitive inhibitors (like imatinib) by targeting a distinct regulatory site, thereby reducing the proliferation of BCR-ABL1-positive leukemic cells.
